subject: Career
title: The Minto Pyramid for Presentations
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Minto Pyramid for Presentations.

hook.text: Barbara Minto at McKinsey revolutionized how consultants present: start with the answer, not the analysis.

buildup.text: The pyramid principle: lead with the conclusion, then support it with key arguments, then provide data.

discovery.text: Most people present bottom-up: data → analysis → conclusion. Busy executives need top-down: conclusion → support.

twist.text: This feels counterintuitive — 'Won't they want to see my work?' No. They want to see your judgment.

climax.text: Structure: 'I recommend X. Three reasons. First… Second… Third… Questions?'

punchline.text: Start with the answer. Let them ask for the proof.

quiz.question: What does the Minto Pyramid Principle say about presentations?
options: Start with the conclusion, then support with arguments
Build up to the conclusion at the end

details.summary: Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle structures communication by starting with the answer, then grouping supporting arguments logically, and finally backing each argument with detailed evidence..
details.whyItMatters: The Pyramid Principle ensures audiences understand the conclusion even if attention wanes. It eliminates the common mistake of building to a punchline that never lands.
takeaways: Start with the answer, then structure supporting arguments below
Group arguments into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive sets
Each level of the pyramid answers a 'why' from the level above

faq.question: How do I apply the Minto Pyramid to a five-minute presentation?
faq.answer: Open with your main recommendation in one sentence. Present two to three key arguments that support it. For each argument, offer one piece of evidence. This gives you a clean three-tier structure that fits within five minutes with time for questions.

faq.question: What is the difference between the Minto Pyramid and BLUF?
faq.answer: BLUF is a communication habit of leading with the conclusion. The Minto Pyramid is a complete structural framework for organizing all the supporting logic beneath that conclusion. BLUF is the tip of the pyramid; Minto is the entire architecture.
